tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: For Assessment Year 2016-17, the case was selected for reassessment. Company had filed a Writ Petition before Hon'ble Bombay High Court against notices issued u/s 148A(b) and order passed u/s 148A(d). Hon'ble Bombay High Court decided the matter in favour of the Company and thus, the re-assessment proceedings were quashed as the sanction of approval for re-opening was not received from appropriate authority. Department filed an appeal before Hon'ble Supreme Court. The Hon'ble Supreme Court has set aside the order passed by the Hon'ble Bombay High Court and has directed the Assessing Officers to pass appropriate orders. The amount involved in the said matter is Rs. 1952.56 Lakhs. The case is pending for order giving effect before assessing officer as per the directions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
tax_litigation.status: There is no change in status since last quarter. The case is pending for order giving effect before assessing officer as per the directions of the Hon’ble Supreme Court.

timeline.summary: Pradeep Kumar Kheruka, as promoter of Borosil Renewables, confirmed no encumbrance on equity shares held as of March 31, 2026, under SEBI’s Regulation 31(4).
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹439.92 Cr (+17.8% YoY), net profit ₹169.12 Cr (against a loss of ₹29.53 Cr a year earlier).
Borosil Renewables reported Q4FY26 standalone revenue of ₹438 Cr (+34% YoY) and highlighted its ongoing ₹950 Cr capacity expansion targeted for Dec 2026.
Borosil Renewables filed Q4FY26 monitoring agency reports on May 12, 2026.
BOROSIL RENEWABLES LIMITED shared the audio recording of its May 13, 2026, analysts/institutional investors conference call on its website.
Borosil Renewables reported Q4FY26 standalone revenue of ₹437.62 Cr and EBITDA of ₹144.61 Cr, while announcing an enabling resolution for a ₹750 Cr fundraise.
Pradeep Kumar Kheruka and other promoters of Borosil Renewables Limited declared no substantial shareholding changes under SEBI’s Regulation 31(4) as of March 31, 2026, with no pledges.
Borosil Renewables received a customs show cause notice for ₹13.30 crore regarding capital goods tariff classification.
Borosil Renewables announced the Ministry of Finance's continuation of countervailing duty on solar glass from Malaysia for five years.

On October 17, 2026, Borosil Renewables informed the exchange about a Customs adjudication order levying ₹0.60 crore in total fines and penalties over the tariff classification of imported project machinery.
